claim: Bicarbonate secretion is a fundamental process involved in maintaining acid-base homeostasis.
source: Bicarbonate secretion is a fundamental process involved in maintaining acid-base homeostasis.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about bicarbonate's role in physiology.

claim: Disruption of bicarbonate entry into airway lumen produces several defects in lung function due to thick mucus accumulation.
source: Disruption of bicarbonate entry into airway lumen, as has been observed in cystic fibrosis, produces several defects in lung function due to thick mucus accumulation.
evidence: This statement references observations in cystic fibrosis, drawing from established knowledge and citations.

claim: Bicarbonate is critical for correct mucin deployment.
source: Bicarbonate is critical for correct mucin deployment
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about bicarbonate's role in mucin function.

claim: CFTR and TMEM16A function as apical anion exit channels in mammalian airways.
source: The current model of anion secretion in mammalian airways consists of CFTR and TMEM16A as apical anion exit channels
evidence: This describes the current model based on existing scientific literature.

claim: CFTR and TMEM16A have limited capacity for bicarbonate transport compared to chloride.
source: CFTR and TMEM16A as apical anion exit channels, with limited capacity for bicarbonate transport compared to chloride.
evidence: This is stated as part of the current model of anion secretion.

claim: CFTR and TMEM16A can couple to SLC26A4 anion exchanger to maximise bicarbonate secretion.
source: However, both channels can couple to SLC26A4 anion exchanger to maximise bicarbonate secretion.
evidence: This describes a known mechanism from existing literature.

claim: Current models lack details about the identity of basolateral protein(s) responsible for bicarbonate uptake into airway epithelial cells.
source: Nevertheless, current models lack any details about the identity of the basolateral protein(s) responsible for bicarbonate uptake into airway epithelial cells.
evidence: This identifies a gap in current scientific knowledge.

claim: The electrogenic, sodium-dependent, bicarbonate cotransporter, SLC4A4, is expressed in the basolateral membrane of human and mouse airways.
source: We report herein that the electrogenic, sodium-dependent, bicarbonate cotransporter, SLC4A4, is expressed in the basolateral membrane of human and mouse airways
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data including immunolocalization (Figure 2G,H) and functional studies.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of SLC4A4 reduces bicarbonate secretion.
source: it's pharmacological inhibition or genetic silencing reduces bicarbonate secretion
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from Ussing chamber experiments (Figure 1) and ASL pH measurements (Figure 2).

claim: Genetic silencing of SLC4A4 reduces bicarbonate secretion.
source: it's pharmacological inhibition or genetic silencing reduces bicarbonate secretion
evidence: This is supported by data from Slc4a4-/- mice experiments (Figure 4).

claim: SLC4A4 inhibition induced an acidification of the airways surface liquid in fully differentiated primary human airway cells cultures.
source: In fully differentiated primary human airway cells cultures, SLC4A4 inhibition induced an acidification of the airways surface liquid
evidence: This is supported by ASL pH measurement data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: SLC4A4 inhibition markedly reduced the capacity of cells to recover from an acid load.
source: markedly reduced the capacity of cells to recover from an acid load
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH recovery experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: Slc4a4-null mice have a previously unreported lung phenotype characterized by mucus accumulation.
source: Studies in the Slc4a4 -null mice revealed a previously unreported lung phenotype, characterized by mucus accumulation
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Slc4a4-null mice have reduced mucociliary clearance.
source: Studies in the Slc4a4 -null mice revealed a previously unreported lung phenotype, characterized by mucus accumulation and reduced mucociliary clearance.
evidence: This is supported by mucociliary clearance measurements shown in Figure 4H,I.

claim: Reduction of SLC4A4 function induced a CF-like phenotype even when chloride secretion remained intact.
source: our results demonstrate that the reduction of SLC4A4 function induced a CF-like phenotype, even when chloride secretion remained intact
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing mucus accumulation and reduced mucociliary clearance in Slc4a4-/- mice.

claim: SLC4A4 plays an important role in bicarbonate secretion and mammalian airway function.
source: highlighting the important role SLC4A4 plays in bicarbonate secretion and mammalian airway function
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the collective experimental results.

claim: Cystic fibrosis is the most common autosomal recessive disease in humans.
source: cystic fibrosis (CF), the most common, autosomal recessive, disease in humans
evidence: This is established medical knowledge about cystic fibrosis.

claim: Impaired chloride secretion reduces the volume of the airway surface liquid.
source: Impaired Cl- secretion reduces the volume of the fluid that covers the airway epithelium, the airway surface liquid (ASL)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work (Cantin et al., 2006; Saint-Criq and Gray, 2017).

claim: Reduced airway surface liquid volume leads to ciliary dysfunction and promotes mucus stasis and airway obstruction.
source: leading to ciliary dysfunction and promoting mucus stasis and airway obstruction
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Deficient bicarbonate secretion reduces ASL pH which compromises post-secretory mucin maturation and clearance.
source: Deficient HCO3- secretion reduces ASL pH which compromises post-secretory mucin maturation and clearance
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hoegger et al., 2014.

claim: Deficient bicarbonate secretion impairs the antimicrobial function of epithelial cells.
source: impairs the antimicrobial function of epithelial cells
evidence: This is supported by citations to Pezzulo et al., 2012 and Shah et al., 2016.

claim: Deficient bicarbonate secretion increases fluid absorption, further decreasing ASL hydration.
source: increases fluid absorption, further decreasing ASL hydration
evidence: This is supported by citation to Garland et al., 2013.

claim: Direct measurement of pH in the distal airways of CF children showed no acidification of the ASL.
source: Whilst direct measurement of pH in the distal airways of CF children showed no acidification of the ASL
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schultz et al., 2017.

claim: Addition of bicarbonate induced an increase in ASL height in human airway epithelial cells cultures.
source: it has been demonstrated that the addition of HCO3- induced an increase in ASL height in human airway epithelial cells (hAECs) cultures
evidence: This is supported by citation to Garland et al., 2013.

claim: Addition of bicarbonate restored the normal properties of mucus from CF patients.
source: restored the normal properties of mucus from CF patients
evidence: This is supported by citations to Garland et al., 2013 and Stigliani et al., 2016.

claim: Aerosolized bicarbonate into CF-pig airways increased bacterial killing.
source: the use of aerosolized HCO3- into CF-pig airways increased bacterial killing
evidence: This is supported by citations to Pezzulo et al., 2012 and Kim et al., 2021.

claim: Bicarbonate supplementation can correct inherent defects of CF in the airways.
source: clearly indicating that HCO3- supplementation can correct inherent defects of CF in the airways
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited studies on bicarbonate supplementation.

claim: Bicarbonate is secreted by CFTR and TMEM16A channels in normal airways.
source: In normal airways, HCO3- is secreted by CFTR and TMEM16A channels
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work (Han et al., 2016; Poulsen et al., 1994).

claim: After inflammatory signalling, bicarbonate secretion is augmented through increased expression of the Cl-/HCO3- exchanger Pendrin (SLC26A4).
source: after inflammatory signalling, HCO3- secretion is augmented through increased expression of the Cl- /HCO3- exchanger Pendrin (SLC26A4)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2019; Rehman et al., 2020; Garnett et al., 2011.

claim: The mechanism of basolateral bicarbonate transport/uptake in native pulmonary tissues is still lacking.
source: the mechanism of basolateral HCO3- transport/uptake in native pulmonary tissues is still lacking
evidence: This identifies a gap in current knowledge.

claim: SLC4A4, SLC4A5, SLC4A7, and SLC4A8 are expressed at mRNA levels in primary hAECs from three different individuals.
source: The use of specific primers (Supplementary file 1) for each NCBT revealed that SLC4A4, SLC4A5, SLC4A7, and SLC4A8 are expressed at mRNA levels in primary hAECs from three different individuals (P1, P2, P3, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-E).
evidence: This is supported by PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-E.

claim: SLC4A10 showed near undetectable level of mRNA expression in primary hAECs.
source: SLC4A10 showed near undetectable level of mRNA expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Isoforms B/C of NBCe1 were more highly expressed than isoform A in primary hAECs.
source: isoforms B/C of NBCe1 (known as the pancreatic isoform, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) were more highly expressed than isoform A (known as the kidney isoform; Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and 1E.

claim: SLC4A4 is the most expressed member of the SLC4A family in primary hAECs, closely followed by SLC4A7, SLC4A8, and SLC4A5.
source: Data extraction from previously published RNA-seq results (Saint-Criq et al., 2020) (GEO series accession number GSE154905) confirmed the pattern of expression of these isoforms (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G) and revealed that SLC4A4 is the most expressed member, closely followed by SLC4A7, SLC4A8, and SLC4A5.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Bestrophins were expressed in primary hAECs but with one to two logs lower than SLC4A4, SLC4A7, and SLC4A8.
source: Other candidate HCO3- transporters such as Bestrophins were also expressed in these cells but with one to two logs lower than SLC4A4, SLC4A7, and SLC4A8 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: In the absence of stimulants, bicarbonate secretion was inhibited by S0859 in primary hAECs.
source: Results, shown in Figure 1 confirmed that, in the absence of stimulants, HCO3- secretion was inhibited by S0859 (Figure 1A and B)
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: S0859 did not have any effect on short-circuit current in the absence of bicarbonate in primary hAECs.
source: this pharmacological inhibitor did not have any effect on short-circuit current (Isc) in the absence of HCO3- (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: S0859 did not reduce Forskolin-stimulated bicarbonate secretion under the tested conditions in primary hAECs.
source: S0859 did not reduce Fsk-stimulated HCO3- secretion (Figure 1C) under these conditions.
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: There is an electrogenic bicarbonate transporter at the basolateral membrane of hAECs.
source: These results show that there is an electrogenic HCO3- transporter at the basolateral membrane of hAECs
evidence: This is inferred from the Ussing chamber experiments showing S0859-sensitive currents.

claim: The electrogenic bicarbonate transporter at the basolateral membrane of hAECs is consistent with SLC4A4.
source: which is consistent with SLC4A4, since SLC4A7 and SLC4A8 are electroneutral (Parker and Boron, 2013), and SLC4A5 has been shown to be localized to the apical membrane of renal epithelial cells and cholangiocytes
evidence: This is inferred from the electrogenic properties and citations about other SLC4 family members.

claim: Exposing hAECs bilaterally to a HCO3-/CO2-gassed KRB solution induced a transient acidification.
source: As shown in Figure 1E, exposing cells bilaterally to a HCO3-/CO2-gassed KRB solution induced a transient acidification.
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Apical-only CO2 exposure in the absence of basolateral bicarbonate induced a sustained acidification in hAECs.
source: an apical-only CO2 exposure, in the absence of basolateral HCO3-, induced a sustained acidification (of the same amplitude as with bilateral HCO3-/CO2, Figure 1F and H)
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 1F and H.

claim: pHi recovery in hAECs occurred when bicarbonate was re-introduced basolaterally after CO2-induced acidification.
source: that recovered when HCO3- was re-introduced basolaterally (Figure 1F,I).
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 1F and I.

claim: pHi recovery in hAECs depended on the presence of Na+ in the basolateral solution.
source: This pHi recovery depended on the presence of Na+ in the basolateral solution (Figure 1G)
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: S0859 blocked the pHi recovery from CO2-induced acidification in hAECs.
source: which was confirmed using S0859 which blocked the pHi recovery from the CO2-induced acidification.
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data.

claim: S0859 significantly decreased the rate of pHi recovery from CO2-induced acidification in the presence of NHE inhibitor DMA.
source: In this condition, S0859 still significantly decreased the rate of pHi recovery from the CO2-induced acidification (Figure 1J and K).
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 1J and K.

claim: NBCe1 inhibition significantly decreased ASL pH under resting conditions with a t1/2 of 46 min.
source: NBCe1 inhibition significantly decreased ASL pH under resting conditions with a t1/2 of 46 min (Figure 2A,B)
evidence: This is supported by ASL pH measurement data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: S0859 partially prevented the Forskolin-induced increase in ASL pH.
source: partially prevented the Fsk-induced increase in ASL pH which we have previously shown was via CFTR (Delpiano et al., 2018; Saint-Criq et al., 2019; Figure 2C,D)
evidence: This is supported by ASL pH measurement data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: S0859 increased the half-time response to Forskolin from 25 to 31 min in ASL pH measurements.
source: increasing the half-time response to Fsk from 25 to 31 min.
evidence: This is supported by ASL pH measurement data.

claim: S0859 significantly reduced the Forskolin-induced, CFTR-dependent, increase in ASL pH with a half-time of 14 min when added after Forskolin.
source: when S0859 was added after Fsk, it significantly reduced the Fsk-induced, CFTR-dependent, increase in ASL pH with a half-time of 14 min (Figure 2E,F)
evidence: This is supported by ASL pH measurement data shown in Figure 2E,F.

claim: SLC4A4 cotransporter plays a central role in ASL pH homeostasis under both resting and stimulated conditions.
source: confirming the central role of SLC4A4 cotransporter in ASL pH homeostasis under both resting and stimulated conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the ASL pH measurement data.

claim: SLC4A4 locates in the basolateral membrane of acetylated tubulin positive human airway epithelial cells.
source: SLC4A4 locates in the basolateral membrane of acetylated tubulin (Ac-tubulin) positive human airway epithelial cells.
evidence: This is supported by immunolocalization data shown in Figure 2G,H.

claim: SLC4A4 is preferentially expressed in ciliated cells in human airways.
source: immunolocalization of SLC4A4 protein in human airway tissues showed intracellular and basolateral membrane staining in epithelial cells that were also positively stained for acetylated-tubulin indicating that SLC4A4 is preferentially expressed in ciliated cells in human airways (Figure 2G,H).
evidence: This is supported by immunolocalization data shown in Figure 2G,H.

claim: Slc4a4, Slc4a5, Slc4a7, and Slc4a10 were expressed in epithelial cells from mouse tracheas.
source: we performed RT-PCR of epithelial cells from mouse tracheas and observed that several members of the SLC4 family including Slc4a4, Slc4a5, Slc4a7, and Slc4a10 were expressed (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 A-E).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 A-E.

claim: Slc4a4 isoform B/C but not isoform A was expressed in mouse airways.
source: Studies of Slc4a4 isoforms demonstrated that isoform B/C but not isoform A was expressed in mouse airways (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: UTP-induced anion current was significantly reduced in the absence of bicarbonate in mouse trachea.
source: Ussing chamber experiments performed in freshly excised mouse trachea using HCO3- (Figure 3A) or HEPES (Figure 3B) buffered solutions, showed that UTP-induced an anion current that was significantly reduced in the absence of HCO3- (–138±28 to -82±15 µA cm–2; p<0.01 Mann-Whitney test)
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: Absence of bicarbonate had no significant effect on the cAMP-induced anion secretion in mouse trachea.
source: but no significant effect on the cAMP-induced anion secretion, or the amiloride-sensitive sodium absorption (Figure 3C) was detected
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: De novo synthesis of bicarbonate was not participating in the UTP-induced electrogenic anion secretion in mouse trachea.
source: Complementary studies in HCO3- buffer showed that de novo synthesis of HCO3- was not participating in the UTP-induced electrogenic anion secretion, as incubation of tracheas with acetazolamide didn't affect the magnitude of the UTP-induced current (–124±14 µA cm–2; p>0.05 One-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber experiments with acetazolamide.

claim: S0859 inhibited the cAMP-induced anion current in mouse trachea.
source: Using the SLC4A4 blocker S0859, we observed the inhibition of the cAMP-induced anion current (ΔIsc –12.2±2.4 µA cm–2) suggesting that SLC4A4 might participate in the cAMP-response (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-C).
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: Basal bicarbonate secretion occurs in mouse trachea.
source: confirming that electrogenic-bicarbonate secretion was not significantly stimulated by cAMP, indicating that basal HCO3- secretion occurs in mouse trachea.
evidence: This is inferred from the Ussing chamber experiments showing S0859-sensitive basal currents.

claim: S0859 reduced basal current only in bicarbonate buffer in mouse trachea.
source: To confirm this last hypothesis we added S0589 to tissues pre-incubated with amiloride and observed a reduction in the basal current only in HCO3- buffer (–13.9±3.3 to -3.0±1.6 Δ µA cm–2 for HCO3- vs HEPES buffer; p<0.02; Mann-Whitney; Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 3D–F.

claim: UTP-induced anion secretion in mouse tracheas maintained in bicarbonate buffer was significantly reduced by previous addition of S0859.
source: As can be observed (Figure 3G and H) the UTP-induced anion secretion in tracheas maintained in HCO3- buffer was significantly reduced by previous addition of S0859 (–368±25 to -200±17 µA cm–2; p<0.001 One-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 3G and H.

claim: UTP response was reduced when bicarbonate was replaced with HEPES buffer in mouse trachea.
source: The UTP response was also reduced when HCO3- was replaced with HEPES buffer (Figure 3I) (–199±25 µA cm–2; p<0.001 One-way ANOVA)
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Addition of S0859 induced no significant reduction of the UTP-induced anion secretion in mouse tissues maintained in HEPES buffer.
source: but the addition of S0859 induced no significant reduction of the UTP-induced anion secretion in tissues maintained in HEPES buffer (Figure 3J) (–142±12 µA cm–2; p>0.05 One-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 3J.

claim: UTP induced an intracellular acidification in murine airway cells.
source: As shown in Figure 3L, UTP induced an intracellular acidification (ΔpHi –0.25±0.02)
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 3L.

claim: UTP-induced intracellular acidification was significantly reduced when murine airway cells were placed in low Cl- buffer.
source: that was significantly reduced when cells were placed in low Cl- buffer (ΔpHi –0.11±0.02), indicating the existence of Cl-/HCO3- exchange.
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data.

claim: UTP was almost unable to induce intracellular acidification in absence of bicarbonate in murine airway cells.
source: Figure 3M summarizes changes in intracellular pH and includes experiments in HEPES buffer, which shows that UTP was almost unable to induce intracellular acidification (ΔpHi –0.01±0.01) in absence of HCO3-.
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 3M.

claim: S0859 induced acidification of the intracellular compartment and prevented UTP-induced acidification in murine airway cells.
source: To test if the UTP-induced intracellular acidification was dependent on SLC4A4 activity, we tested the S0859 inhibitor and observed acidification of the intracellular compartment and prevention of UTP-induced acidification (Figure 3—figure supplement 2G-H).
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2G-H.

claim: Washout of S0859 partially restored pHi and UTP-induced acidification in murine airway cells.
source: Washout of S0859 partially restored pHi and UTP-induced acidification. (Figure 3—figure supplement 2G-H; –0.05±0.01 to -0.13±0.03 ΔpHi, for UTP with S0559 and UTP post washout, respectively; p>0.002; Mann-Whitney).
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2G-H.

claim: Both basal and UTP-induced bicarbonate secretion are dependent on SLC4A4 activity in mouse airway epithelial cells.
source: These data suggest that both basal and UTP-induced HCO3- secretion are dependent on SLC4A4 activity in mouse airway epithelial cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the intracellular pH and Ussing chamber data.

claim: Slc4a4-/- animals were affected by defects in tracheal cartilage formation with the presence of ventral gaps and abnormal patterns on the rostrocaudal side.
source: First, we observed that Slc4a4-/- animals were affected by defects in tracheal cartilage formation with the presence of ventral gaps and abnormal patterns on the rostrocaudal side (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: In wild-type animals, SLC4A4 showed strong localization in the airway epithelium but the signal was nearly absent in the airways from the Slc4a4-/- mice.
source: In wild-type animals, immunolocalization of SLC4A4 showed strong localization in the airway epithelium but the signal was nearly absent in the airways from the Slc4a4-/- mice (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by immunolocalization data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: SLC4A4 was preferentially expressed in CCSP-positive cells that correspond to Club cells in mouse airways.
source: Using the same antibody, we showed that SLC4A4 was preferentially expressed in CCSP-positive cells that correspond to Club cells
evidence: This is supported by immunolocalization data.

claim: SLC4A4 was excluded from cells positive to acetylated-Tubulin that identify ciliated cells in mouse airways.
source: and was excluded from cells positive to acetylated-Tubulin, that identify ciliated cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by immunolocalization data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The pattern of SLC4A4 expression was maintained in distal airway bronchi and bronchioles in mouse.
source: This pattern of expression was maintained in distal airway bronchi and bronchioles (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by immunolocalization data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Histological examination of the Slc4a4-/- mouse airways demonstrated the presence of adherent mucus at the surface of the tracheal epithelium.
source: Further histological examination of the Slc4a4-/- mouse airways demonstrated the presence of adherent mucus at the surface of the tracheal epithelium (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D)
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Adherent mucus was present in the bronchi of Slc4a4-/- mice.
source: as well as in the bronchi (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E-G)
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E-G.

claim: Adherent mucus was present in the bronchioli of Slc4a4-/- mice.
source: and bronchioli (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Signs of damaged epithelium was observed as interruptions in the epithelial layer facing the lumen in the Slc4a4-/- airways.
source: Signs of damaged epithelium was also observed as interruptions in the epithelial layer facing the lumen in the Slc4a4-/- airways (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1F,H)
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1F,H.

claim: Slc4a4-/- tracheas had decreased Rte that prevented electrophysiological measurements.
source: that might explain the decreased Rte of the tracheas placed in Ussing chambers and that prevented electrophysiological measurements in the Slc4a4-/- tracheas (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by Ussing chamber data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: A decrease in the magnitude of intracellular acidification was observed in Slc4a4-/- cells when compared to wild type animals during UTP stimulation.
source: We observed a decrease in the magnitude of intracellular acidification in Slc4a4-/- cells when compared to those from wild type animals during UTP stimulation (–0.24±0.01 to -0.14±0.01 ΔpH[i], for wild type vs Slc4a4-/-)
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 4F–G.

claim: An important amount of bicarbonate accumulates in airways cells via SLC4A4.
source: suggesting that an important amount of HCO3- accumulates in airways cells via SLC4A4 (Figure 4F–G).
evidence: This is inferred from the reduced UTP-induced acidification in Slc4a4-/- cells.

claim: After UTP wash-out, the acidification persisted in the wild type cells but not in the Slc4a4-/-.
source: We also noticed that after UTP wash-out, the acidification persisted in the wild type cells but not in the Slc4a4-/- (Figure 4—figure supplement 1J; –0.09±0.02 to -0.02±0.01 ΔpH[i], for wild type vs Slc4a4-/-)
evidence: This is supported by intracellular pH measurement data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1J.

claim: Bicarbonate secretion was sustained by SLC4A4 activity after UTP wash-out.
source: suggesting that HCO3- secretion was sustained by SLC4A4 activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the persistent acidification in wild type but not Slc4a4-/- cells after UTP wash-out.

claim: Plastic beads covered a larger distance in wild type tissues compared to Slc4a4-/- trachea.
source: As shown in the polar plots in Figure 4H the plastic beads covered a larger distance in wild type tissues
evidence: This is supported by mucociliary clearance data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Retrograde movement of beads was observed in some Slc4a4-/- trachea.
source: and, in some cases, retrograde movement of beads was observed in the Slc4a4-/- trachea.
evidence: This is an observation from the mucociliary clearance experiments.

claim: A similar reduction in distance travelled was observed in wild type tissues bathed in HEPES buffer.
source: A similar reduction in distance travelled was observed in wild type tissues bathed in HEPES buffer.
evidence: This is supported by mucociliary clearance data.

claim: The use of HEPES buffer in the Slc4a4-/- tracheas showed no further effect on both speed and total distance travelled by the beads.
source: The use of HEPES buffer in the Slc4a4-/- tracheas showed no further effect on both speed and total distance travelled by the beads.
evidence: This is supported by mucociliary clearance data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Mucociliary clearance is significantly decreased when bicarbonate transport is impaired after Slc4a4 silencing.
source: This data set demonstrates that mucociliary clearance is significantly decreased when HCO3- transport is impaired after Slc4a4 silencing.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mucociliary clearance data.

claim: Early characterization in canine and human airway epithelium indicated that bicarbonate secretion occurs via CFTR, is activated by cAMP and dependent on basolateral Na+.
source: Early characterization in canine and human airway epithelium indicated that HCO3- secretion occurs via CFTR, is activated by cAMP and dependent on basolateral Na+ Smith and Welsh, 1992
evidence: This is supported by citation to Smith and Welsh, 1992.

claim: Similar features of bicarbonate secretion were observed in the Calu-3 cell line.
source: similar features were observed in the Calu-3 cell line (Devor et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Devor et al., 1999.

claim: Bicarbonate secretion in the mouse airways is mostly Ca2+ rather than cAMP-activated.
source: Nevertheless, and in contrast to human airway epithelium, our present data shows that HCO3- secretion in the mouse airways is mostly Ca+2- rather than cAMP-activated
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Ussing chamber experiments in mouse trachea.

claim: Both human and mouse share a basal secretory component for bicarbonate.
source: but both human and mouse share a basal secretory component for HCO3- previously observed in human bronchioles (Shamsuddin and Quinton, 2019), and that we now show is dependent on SLC4A4 activity.
evidence: This is supported by data from both human and mouse experiments and citation to Shamsuddin and Quinton, 2019.

claim: Basolateral localization of SLC4A4 was previously demonstrated in the Calu-3 cell line.
source: Basolateral localization of SLC4A4 was previously demonstrated in the Calu-3 cell line (Kreindler et al., 2006)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kreindler et al., 2006.

claim: Human airways express SLC4A4 in ciliated cells preferentially.
source: Here, we demonstrate that human airways express SLC4A4 in ciliated cells preferentially
evidence: This is supported by immunolocalization data shown in Figure 2G,H.

claim: The observed basolateral localization of SLC4A4 correlates with the functional evidence provided.
source: and that the observed basolateral localization correlates with the functional evidence provided, reinforcing the role SLC4A4 in basolateral HCO3- transport into the cells.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the localization data with functional data.

claim: Apical CFTR is necessary for bicarbonate secretion.
source: Nevertheless, it must be considered that the sole expression of SLC4A4 does not assure HCO3- secretion as compelling evidence has demonstrated that apical CFTR is also necessary.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: TMEM16A channel has been shown to be expressed in goblet cells.
source: While the calcium-activated TMEM16A channel has been shown to be expressed in goblet cells (Scudieri et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Scudieri et al., 2012.

claim: Both bicarbonate transporters, CFTR and pendrin, have been localized in the apical membrane of ciliated hAECs cells.
source: both HCO3- transporters, CFTR and pendrin, have been localized in the apical membrane of ciliated hAECs cells supporting our observation (Kim et al., 2019; Kreda et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2019 and Kreda et al., 2005.

claim: SLC4A4-B, and not the isoform A, is functionally coupled to CFTR through the IRBIT protein in pancreatic ducts.
source: Moreover, it has been demonstrated that SLC4A4-B, that we detected in human and mouse, and not the isoform A, is functionally coupled to CFTR through the IRBIT protein in pancreatic ducts (Yang et al., 2009; Shirakabe et al., 2006)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Yang et al., 2009 and Shirakabe et al., 2006.

claim: A functional coupling in the same cell type is necessary for efficient bicarbonate secretion.
source: further supporting the idea that a functional coupling in the same cell type is necessary for efficient HCO3- secretion.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited studies on functional coupling.

claim: CFTR and Pendrin expression increases in secretory cells after cytokine stimulation.
source: Even though, CFTR and Pendrin expression increases in secretory cells after cytokine stimulation, SLC4A4 remained unaltered
evidence: This is stated as an observation from previous studies.

claim: Other basolateral bicarbonate transporter support bicarbonate secretion in human secretory cells during the inflammatory response.
source: suggesting that other basolateral HCO3- transporter support HCO3- secretion in human secretory cells during the inflammatory response (Rehman et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation that SLC4A4 remained unaltered, supported by citation to Rehman et al., 2020.

claim: The pulmonary ionocyte is a rare airway epithelial cell type that contains the highest amount of CFTR/Cftr transcripts in human and mouse.
source: CFTR distribution in airway epithelium has been under renewed scrutiny after the recent discovery of the pulmonary ionocyte, a rare airway epithelial cell type that contains the highest amount of CFTR/Cftr transcripts in human and mouse (Montoro et al., 2018; Plasschaert et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Montoro et al., 2018 and Plasschaert et al., 2018.

claim: Most human airway epithelial cell types express CFTR including ciliated cells.
source: Nevertheless, recent and detailed studies demonstrate that most human airway epithelial cell types express CFTR including ciliated cells as was initially demonstrated (Engelhardt et al., 1994; Okuda et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Engelhardt et al., 1994 and Okuda et al., 2021.

claim: SLC4A4 localization in mouse was different from human airway epithelium, as the mouse SLC4A4 was expressed in CCSP+ and not ciliated cells.
source: We noticed that SLC4A4 localization in mouse was different from human airway epithelium, as the mouse SLC4A4 was expressed in CCSP +and not ciliated cells.
evidence: This is supported by immunolocalization data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: CFTR and TMEM16A channels were specifically located in non-ciliated cells of mouse airways.
source: Previously, CFTR and TMEM16A channels were specifically located in non-ciliated cells of mouse airways (Hahn et al., 2018), a distribution also conserved in the rat (Hahn et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hahn et al., 2018 and Hahn et al., 2017.

claim: Pendrin was detected in non-ciliated secretory MUC5AC+ cells in mouse airways.
source: Pendrin, was also detected in non-ciliated secretory MUC5AC + cells
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jia et al., 2016.

claim: A functional coupling for bicarbonate secretion occurs in secretory non-ciliated cells of the mouse airways.
source: suggesting that a functional coupling for HCO3- secretion occurs in secretory non-ciliated cells of the mouse airways (Jia et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the localization data, supported by citation to Jia et al., 2016.

claim: CFTR is not the principal chloride transporter in the mouse airways.
source: for example CFTR, is not the principal Cl- transporter in the mouse airways
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about mouse airways.

claim: Silencing or mutation of Cftr in mice did not produce CF disease of the lungs.
source: and consequently silencing or mutation of Cftr in mice did not produce CF disease of the lungs (Ratcliff et al., 1993; Snouwaert et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ratcliff et al., 1993 and Snouwaert et al., 1992.

claim: The ATP12A H+/K+ ATPase is expressed in human and not mouse airways.
source: Furthermore, the expression in human and not mouse airways of another protein that influence ASL pH, the ATP12A H+/K+ ATPase
evidence: This is stated as a known difference between human and mouse airways.

claim: The ATP12A H+/K+ ATPase magnifies ASL acidification in human airways in CF disease.
source: magnifies ASL acidification in human airways in CF disease (Shah et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Shah et al., 2016.

claim: Silencing of Tmem16a in the mouse affected both chloride and bicarbonate secretion.
source: Previous observations obtained by inducing silencing of Tmem16a in the mouse, or using cells carrying natural mutations in CFTR, affected both Cl- and HCO3- secretion
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of previous studies.

claim: Using cells carrying natural mutations in CFTR affected both chloride and bicarbonate secretion.
source: or using cells carrying natural mutations in CFTR, affected both Cl- and HCO3- secretion making it difficult to understand what the consequences of reduced transport for each anion alone are
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of previous studies, supported by citation to Gorrieri et al., 2016 and Rock et al., 2009.

claim: The silencing of Slc4a4 induced a muco-obstructive phenotype in the mouse.
source: As observed here, the silencing of Slcl4a4 induced a muco-obstructive phenotype in the mouse
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The silencing of Slc12a2, which encodes the bumetanide-sensitive NKCC1 co-transporter, did not induce a muco-obstructive phenotype in the mouse.
source: whereas the silencing of Slc12a2, which encodes the bumetanide-sensitive NKCC1 co-transporter, which is essential for Cl- accumulation and secretion, did not (Grubb et al., 2001)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Grubb et al., 2001.

claim: Lack of bicarbonate is pathologically more relevant than chloride secretion in mouse airways.
source: suggesting that lack of HCO3- is pathologically more relevant than Cl- secretion in mouse airways.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the phenotypes of Slc4a4-/- and Slc12a2-/- mice.

claim: hAEC from CF patients produce acidic ASL and mucus that is more viscous than in cells from non-CF donors.
source: For example, hAEC from CF patients produce acidic ASL and mucus that is more viscous than in cells from non-CF donors (Tang et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tang et al., 2016.

claim: The acidification of the ASL induced abnormal epithelial immune responses and reduced MCC that could be reversed after bicarbonate supplementation.
source: the acidification of the ASL induced abnormal epithelial immune responses and reduced MCC that could be reversed after HCO3- supplementation (Pezzulo et al., 2012; Shah et al., 2016; Ferrera et al., 2021; Simonin et al., 2019; Birket et al., 2018; Cooper et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Bicarbonate secretion is necessary for proper mucus release from hAECs.
source: Furthermore, HCO3- secretion is necessary for proper mucus release from hAECs (Gorrieri et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gorrieri et al., 2016.

claim: Bicarbonate secretion is necessary for maintenance of normal amounts of ENaC-mediated Na+ absorption and ASL volume.
source: and maintenance of normal amounts of ENaC-mediated Na+ absorption and ASL volume (Garland et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Garland et al., 2013.

claim: The reduction of bicarbonate transport after SLC4A4 inhibition is consistent with the expected muco-obstructive phenotype, including reduced MCC and mucus accumulation.
source: Even though technically challenging issues prevented us from measuring ASL pH in the mouse trachea, the reduction of HCO3- transport demonstrated here after SLC4A4 inhibition is consistent with the expected muco-obstructive phenotype, including reduced MCC and mucus accumulation.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the observed phenotype with the expected consequences of reduced bicarbonate transport.

claim: The Slc4a4-null animal and the Slc4a4W516X/W516X avatar mouse are affected by severe metabolic acidosis due to proximal renal tubular acidosis.
source: The Slc4a4-null animal, corresponding to the one used in the present studies, and the Slc4a4W516X/W516X avatar mouse engineered to mimic a non-sense mutation found in a human patient, are affected by severe metabolic acidosis due to proximal renal tubular acidosis (pRTA; Gawenis et al., 2007; Lo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gawenis et al., 2007 and Lo et al., 2011.

claim: Decreased plasma bicarbonate is observed in the Slc4a4-/- mice.
source: Even though, decreased plasma HCO3- is observed in the Slc4a4-/- mice (5.3±0.5 mM; Gawenis et al., 2007)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gawenis et al., 2007.

claim: Reduced bicarbonate availability is unlikely to have influenced mucus accumulation in the airways of Slc4a4-/- mice.
source: is unlikely that reduced HCO3- availability influenced mucus accumulation in the airways, as we have previously determined that the transporter is fully saturated at 3 mM HCO3- (Theparambil et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference based on previous data about transporter saturation, supported by citation to Theparambil et al., 2014.

claim: Extra-renal manifestations of Slc4a4 silencing in the mouse include growth retardation, ocular band keratopathy, splenomegaly, abnormal dentition and intestinal obstructions.
source: Extra-renal manifestations of Slc4a4 silencing in the mouse include growth retardation, ocular band keratopathy, splenomegaly, abnormal dentition and intestinal obstructions
evidence: This is stated as known phenotypes from previous studies.

claim: Most extra-renal manifestations of Slc4a4 silencing in the mouse mimic the clinical findings observed in human patients.
source: most of which mimics the clinical findings observed in human patients.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison between mouse and human phenotypes.

claim: Lung defects have not been reported in human patients with SLC4A4 mutations.
source: Nevertheless lung defects have not been reported in human patients
evidence: This is stated as an observation about human clinical reports.

claim: Human disease related to SLC4A4 mutations is milder than in mouse models.
source: and observation which could be explained by the fact that human disease is milder than in mouse models.
evidence: This is speculation about why lung defects are not reported in humans.

claim: At birth human kidneys are functionally more mature than in mouse.
source: This might be related to the fact that at birth human kidneys are functionally more mature than in mouse (Takahashi et al., 2000)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Takahashi et al., 2000.

claim: Heterozygous Slc4a4 animals present mild pRTA.
source: and for example, while heterozygous animals present mild pRTA
evidence: This is stated as an observation from mouse studies.

claim: Human patients bearing heterozygous SLC4A4 mutations did not show any signs of disease.
source: human patients bearing heterozygous SLC4A4 mutations did not show any signs of disease (Gawenis et al., 2007; Lo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gawenis et al., 2007 and Lo et al., 2011.

claim: Compensatory activity of other Na+-coupled bicarbonate cotransporters or exchangers has been discarded in mouse.
source: Even though, a compensatory activity of other Na+-coupled HCO3- cotransporters, or exchangers, has been discarded in mouse
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous studies.

claim: Compensatory activity of other Na+-coupled bicarbonate cotransporters or exchangers has not been examined in humans.
source: this possibility has not been examined in humans where compensatory activity might benefit patient's health (Lo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is speculation about a possibility that has not been investigated, supported by citation to Lo et al., 2011.

claim: Both the Slc4a4-/- and W516X-mutant animals die soon after weaning.
source: Both the Slc4a4-/- and W516X-mutant animals die soon after weaning as we also observed
evidence: This is supported by the authors' observations and previous studies.

claim: The specific knock-out mouse for SLC4A4 isoform A (NBCe1-A) has a normal life span.
source: but while the specific knock-out mouse for SLC4A4 isoform A (NBCe1-A) has a normal life span
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous studies.

claim: The knock-out mouse for SLC4A4 isoforms B and C (NBCe1-B/C) is still lethal.
source: the knock-out mouse for SLC4A4 isoforms B and C (NBCe1-B/C) is still lethal.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous studies, supported by citation to Salerno et al., 2019 and Lee et al., 2018.

claim: The cause of death of the Slc4a4-/- animals was not due to metabolic acidosis, but rather due to extra renal phenotypes worsened by pRTA.
source: This suggests that the cause of death of the animals was not due to metabolic acidosis, but rather due to extra renal phenotypes worsened by pRTA (Salerno et al., 2019; Lee et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the differential lethality of different knockout models, supported by citations.

claim: Lethality in Slc4a4-/- mice might be linked to the influence of modifier genes.
source: This observation might also be linked to the influence of modifier genes as observed in human patients and CF mouse models (Rozmahel et al., 1996; Cutting, 2010; Philp et al., 2018).
evidence: This is speculation supported by citations to studies on modifier genes.

claim: Lethality of Slc4a4-/- mice is dependent on the genetic background of the animals.
source: In this regard, our observation that lethality is dependent on the genetic background of the animals supports such a possibility.
evidence: This is supported by the authors' observations shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-B.
